chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Sabbah! Buying the flour is a disgrace, and buying the wheat is an honour, and buying the bread is poverty. We seek Refuge with Allah from the poverty.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of buying wheat versus flour or bread according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the economic stages of grain processing as a metaphor for social dignity, teaching that buying raw wheat signifies self-sufficiency and honor, while purchasing ready-made bread indicates dependency and poverty. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *istighna* (self-sufficiency) and the virtue of adding value through one's own labor rather than relying on others' finished products. The narration encourages believers to seek refuge from the 'poverty' of dependence, aligning material habits with spiritual independence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Al Sabbah! Buying the flour is a disgrace, and buying the wheat is an honour, and buying the bread is poverty. We<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge with Allah<sup>saww</sup> from the poverty’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O abu al-Sabbah, buying flour is humiliation, buying wheat is honor and buying bread is poverty; we seek protection with Allah against poverty.’”
